previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy following a recent ERCP for common bile duct stone removal. The surgery was performed successfully on 2174-09-29. Postoperatively, he experienced right shoulder pain, prompting an orthopedic consultation and joint aspiration, which ruled out recurrent septic arthritis. He also developed transient urinary retention requiring catheterization and was started on tamsulosin, after which he successfully voided with a low post-void residual. His pain was managed with a multimodal regimen, and his liver function tests improved during the stay. He was discharged home on 2174-10-02 in good condition with updated medications and follow-up instructions.
problems: Calculus of gallbladder with other cholecystitis, without mention of obstruction

Brief Hospital Course:
# Anemia: Given known varices, there was concern for 
acute/subacute blood loss. The patient was continued on an IV 
PPI. He was type/screened, with crossmatched packed RBC's. 
Serial hematocrits were checked, with gradual improvement to 34. 
Reticulocyte count was elevated at 3.0. Vital signs reflected 
hemodynamic stability. He did not have any signs of active bleed 
on the floor, and was discharged.

# Weight gain: No indication of left heart failure on exam. 
Likely secondary to non-compliance with diuretics. He had 
reportedly not been taking either furosemide or spironolactone 
for several days, when he was driving long distances on business 
travel. Following this time, the patient reportedly gained 25 
lbs over one week's time. He was given his home spironolactone 
and a single dose of IV lasix equivalent to his home PO regimen, 
and had an excellent urine output within several hours. He was 
discharged with instructions to take his diuretics as previously 
directed.
  
#  Cirrhosis: The patient was continued on his home regimen of 
lactulose and rifaximin. He has follow-up scheduled in the liver 
clinic.

# Thrombocytopenia/Low WBC: Review of old labs revealed that 
thrombocytopenia is chronic, likely realted to Hep C. His WBC 
and Hct seem to correlate. When his Hct has been low in the 
past, it is always associated with low white counts such as the 
one he has currently.

after you received your water pills (diuretics) likely from the 
removal of the extra water.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with known esophageal varices, presenting with
upper GI bleed.

COMPARISON:  CTA abdomen and pelvis ___.

FINDINGS:  The liver is nodular in contour, compatible with cirrhosis.  Within
the right lobe of the liver, possibly segment V, there is an 8-mm rounded
echogenic lesion, without demonstrable color flow.  This is incompletely
characterized.  No additional lesions are identified.  The main, left, and
right portal veins demonstrate directionally appropriate flow.  The main
hepatic artery demonstrates sharp systolic upstrokes and normal diastolic
flow. The hepatic veins are patent.  Patient is status post cholecystectomy. 
There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilatation with the CBD
measuring 2 mm.  A trace amount of perihepatic free fluid is noted.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Cirrhotic liver, with an indeterminate 8-mm echogenic lesion within the
right lobe of the liver, possibly segment V.  This lesion should be further
evaluated with an MRI as hepatocellular carcinoma is not excluded.

2.  Patent portal venous system.

3.  Trace perihepatic free fluid.
